newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Airlines to sell six Airbuses.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Airlines to sell six Airbuses.

text.p: Singapore Airlines (SIA) said on Monday it would put six of its 23 Airbus A310 aircraft up for sale within the next 12 months in line with its policy of selling older aircraft.

An airline spokesman confirmed comments by deputy chairman Cheong Choon Kong, who was quoted on Monday as saying that selling the A310s would be followed by the sale of some Boeing 747-300 combination passenger-cargo plans.
The group sold several Boeing 747-200s in the current financial year ending March 1997, it said.

The Straits Times newspaper quoted Cheong as saying no firm commitments had been received from potential customers for the A310s, which cost the airline US$420 million when they were bought in mid-1983.
Cheong also said SIA would decide this year whether to give less popular long-haul routes to its regional subsidiary SilkAir, a move that should bring major savings.

The alternative, Cheong said, was to abolish first-class seating on SIA flights on the routes. That, Cheong added, would be "logistically simpler" than giving the routes to SilkAir, which now flies short-haul routes.
